title: Cost Center Download Journey — grooming notes
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a lightweight grooming doc for the "Cost Center Download" experience in Console. Focused on: allowing finance/platform teams to produce reconciliable CSVs scoped to cost centers, invoices, and time windows. Connects to budgets/alerts and downstream accounting (ERP).

Why now:
- Customers asking for a single-click CSV that maps tokens/requests to cost centers (tags, routes, billing keys) for month-end reconciliation.
- Current billing export is coarse (per-customer, per-invoice) and forces manual joins.
- This ties into budgets & alerts (users want export filters aligned with budget groupings).

Primary personas:
- Finance analyst (monthly close): expects predictable columns and stable CSV schema, timezone awareness, invoice refs.
- Platform engineer (mapping): wants mappings between Redwood route/model and internal cost centers (tag->cc_id).
- Account admin/owner: sets permissions, triggers exports, uploads to ERP.

Goals (product):
- Provide a reproducible CSV export for cost center reconciliations
- Align export filters with budget groups and alert definitions
- Include enough detail to validate invoice lines without leaking sensitive data

Non-goals:
- Full GL mapping or ERP-specific transformations (we output canonical CSV).
- Real-time streaming; exports are batch by request and delivered via console/email/S3.

High-level flows (wireframe notes):
1) Entry points
   - Billing > Exports > New export (primary)
   - Budgets page > Export matching this budget group (contextual)
   - Invoice detail > Export related ledger (quick export)

2) Core export modal (wireframe fields):
   - Export name (default: "cc-export-YYYYMM")
   - Date range: presets (last month, last 30 days, custom start/end)
   - Timezone for aggregation (UTC default; tenant-local option)
   - Scope selector: checkbox multi-select
       * All invoices in range
       * Specific invoices (search by invoice id)
       * Cost centers (select one or many)
       * Routes / Tags / Models (fuzzy search)
   - Aggregation granularity: line-item, daily summary, invoice-summary
   - Include: token breakdown, request_id, user-provided metadata (labels), invoice_reference
   - Delivery: console-download | email-link | S3 presigned (enter bucket)
   - Permissions: only Account Owners and Billing Admins can run; role-based override for "finance-reads" group
   - File format: CSV (UTF-8), optionally compressed (zip)

3) CSV schema (canonical column set) - explicit sample header:
   "export_timestamp","aggregation_granularity","exported_by","tenant_id","tenant_name","invoice_id","invoice_date","cost_center_id","cc_name","route","model","request_id","request_timestamp","tokens_input","tokens_output","tokens_total","unit_price_per_token_usd","line_amount_usd","currency","notes"

   Example row (comma-delimited):
   2026-02-01T04:05:18Z,daily,true-redwood-account,acct_12345,ACME Corp,inv_2026_001,2026-01-31,cc_42,SearchTeam,route-search,gpt-3.5-turbo,req_98765,2026-01-15T14:00:21Z,120,340,460,0.00002,0.0092,USD,"budget:Q1-search"

   Notes on fields:
   - cost_center_id: canonical id from account settings (not free text). If user hasn't mapped tags to cost centers, "unassigned" used.
   - tokens_* numbers should be integers; unit_price and line_amount are decimal with 6-digit precision max.
   - route/model strings should use canonical internal names to allow automated joins.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- [ ] User can create export with custom date range and scope filters
- [ ] CSV contains header exactly as specified and stable column ordering
- [ ] Export job completes within SLA (small: <2m, medium: <10m, large: async with S3 link) and notifies user
- [ ] Only authorized roles can run/download exports; audit event emitted
- [ ] Export aligns with budget group definitions when started from Budgets page

Backlog (groomed tasks with rough estimates):
- UI: export modal & validations (3d)
- Backend: job API + batch generator (5d)
- CSV schema renderer + tests (2d)
- Permissions + audit (2d)
- Delivery: email presigned + S3 integration (3d)
- Budgets context link + quick-export wiring (2d)
- E2E tests + sample datasets (3d)
- Docs + sample CSV (1d)
- UX: inline mapping helper (map tags -> cost centers) (4d, optional stretch)

Edge cases & decisions for groom/demo:
- Unmapped requests: include cost_center_id = "unassigned" and a separate "mapping_resolution" file in S3 for bulk mapping (can be a follow-up).
- Timezones: store both request_timestamp (UTC) and derived local_date based on tenant preference if requested (store extra column on stretch scope).
- Volume handling: >100k lines should default to S3 delivery; UI shows estimated size before submit.
- PII: redact user email by default unless account-level policy allows; include user_id hashed if needed for reconciliation.

Metrics to watch after launch:
- Number of exports / month (adoption)
- Average processing time (SLA compliance)
- Support tickets related to CSV mismatches (quality)
- Number of customers using budget-linked exports (product signal)

Open questions (needs PM/Legal/Finance):
- Do we need VAT-specific fields or tax breakdown for EU customers? (Legal input)
- Retention policy for generated exports stored in S3 by default (30/90/365 days?).
- Should we version the CSV schema with a header row like "schema_v=1"? (I lean yes for future changes)

UI wireframe sketch notes (for design):
- Modal stepper: 1) scope 2) columns/format 3) delivery & permissions 4) confirm
- Preview button that runs a small sample (first 100 lines) asynchronously and shows sample CSV in modal
- On Budgets page, right rail: "Export reconciliable CSV" -> pre-fills cost center selection

Next steps / owners for demo:
- PM (Maya) to finalize acceptance criteria and answer Open Qs (by 2026-03-05)
- Design (Liam) to produce two mock variants for review (compact vs. guided) by 2026-03-08
- Eng (Evan + Priya) to spike on performance estimate + S3 presigned pattern (by 2026-03-12)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive on CSV columns to reduce churn; if we change a column name later, we should bump schema_v and keep backward compatibility.
- Keep export UI minimal for MVP; more advanced mapping UIs can be iterative follow-ups.

Historical context:
- Builds on prior "Invoice budget export" discussions (see linked artifacts). This doc consolidates cost-center-first workflows requested by finance pilots.

-- end of grooming notes --
